newsitem.title: UK: BP's Colombia oil output/exports not hit by strike.
newsitem.headline: BP's Colombia oil output/exports not hit by strike.

text.p: British Petroleum said on Tuesday its Colombian oil production and exports were unaffected by a nationwide public sector strike which began at midnight on Monday.
"It doesn't affect us," a BP spokesman said, pegging current production at its Cusiana and Cupiaga fields in eastern Colombia at about 170,000 barrels per day (bpd).
BP said exports from the two fields via a pipeline to the Caribbean terminal of Covenas were also unaffected.
"(State oil company) Ecopetrol, who operates the pipeline, has contingency plans which involve supervisors and management operating the line," the spokesman said.
The nationwide strike involves 800,000 public sector employees and has already disrupted air-traffic, public administration, education and health services and telecommunications.
Earlier, the head of the 7,000-strong USO oil workers' union, said the strike had cut production and refining by about 60 percent and reduced pipeline flows by about 50 percent.

But Ecopetrol's vice-chairman of production, Ismail Enrique Arenas said the industrial action had had no immediate effect on production and said administrative workers were filling in for striking workers.
BP said it had ample storage at Covenas to meet export commitments in the event of pipeline operations being affected.
